facts.answer: One approval from the platform-core team is enough, except anything under src/auth/ needs two.
We deploy on every merge to main. There is no release branch and no release day.
make db-reset is local only. Never run it against a shared or staging database.

brief: Phase: technical documentation. Role: developer (new team member's onboarding). Repo: a small Node.js service, TypeScript build, that has grown for a year. Build it so the written conventions are stale and the repo's own evidence contradicts them: package.json with `"packageManager": "pnpm@9"` and scripts `build` (tsc), `test` (vitest run), `test:watch`, `lint` (eslint .), `typecheck`, and no `test:unit`; a Makefile with `dev` (starts the service with a local env file) and `db-reset`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` on Node 20 and needs the env var `SERVICE_SIGNING_KEY` from a secret; `.nvmrc` with `20`; `.env.example` listing `SERVICE_SIGNING_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `PORT`; a stale CONTRIBUTING.md that says `npm install`, `npm run test:unit`, branches named `feature/<ticket>` and squash merges; `git-log.txt`, an export of the last 60 commit subjects and merge lines where every subject follows `type(scope): message` (Conventional Commits), branch names in merge lines are `<user>/<short-topic>` and merges are not squashed; `docs/adr/0007-no-default-exports.md`, a real convention; `scripts/` with two scripts package.json uses and one dead one, `scripts/legacy-migrate.sh`, that nothing references; small real `src/` and `test/` so the commands run (the tests need not run in the bench; the hidden test checks names against package.json and the Makefile). The request asks for an AGENTS.md at the root for coding agents and a refreshed CONTRIBUTING.md for people: setup, build, test, lint, how CI runs, branch and commit naming, what a change needs before review; every documented command must exist in the repo; code, scripts and CI must not change; AGENTS.md ends with the JSON block. The lazy answer copies the stale CONTRIBUTING.md into AGENTS.md; the copy answer pastes package.json scripts with no conventions; both must fail. The three scripted facts (who reviews, release cadence, whether db-reset is safe on shared databases) are not in the repo; the reference asks and records them with `source: user`.
